texts.preamble: Ram Chandra Agarwal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 June, 2025 Author: Anil Kumar Choudhary Bench: Anil Kumar Choudhary (2025:Jhhc:14 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr.M.P. No.1806 of 2023 ------ Ram Chandra Agarwal, Aged about 32 years, S/o Ramesh Kumar Dhanuka, Resident of House No. 1, Nh 33, Near Baba Hotel, Village Charchaka, Dhalbhumgarh, P.O. P.S Dhalbhumgarh, District East Singhbhum ... Petitioner Versus 1. The State of Jharkhand 2. Food Safety Officer, East Singhbhum, P.O. & P.S. Dhalbhum, Jamsedhpur, Dist. East Singhbhum ... Opposite Parties ------ For the Petitioner : Ms. Vani Kumari, Advocate Mr. Prince Pandey, Advocate For the State : Mr. Prabhu Dayal Agrawal, Spl.P.P. ------ Present Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anil Kumar Choudhary By the Court:- Heard the parties. 2. This Criminal Miscellaneous Petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding including the order taking cognizance dated 17.08.2022 in connection with Complaint Case No.5124 of 2022 filed under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 whereby and where under the cognizance has been taken by the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Jamshedpur for the offence punishable under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 against the petitioner. Ram Chandra Agarwal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184209984/ 1 3.
texts.facts: The undisputed fact is that the Food Safety Officer collected the sample of Refined Rice Bran Oil from the shop of the petitioner on 23.08.2021. The same was sent to the laboratory of Food Analyst on 30.08.2021. The Food Analyst submitted his report on 01.10.2021.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner relies upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Madras High Court in the case of S. Sakthivel & Another vs. The State Represented by Food Safety Officer, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration passed in Crl.O.P. (MD) No.5994 of 2019 dated 23.03.2022 and submits that in that case since the mandatory provision of furnishing the report as envisaged under Section 42 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 was not adhered to by the Food Analyst, the entire criminal proceeding, being bad in law, was [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Therefore, it is submitted that in this case also there being violation of mandatory requirement of law under Section 42 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, hence, the prayer, as prayed for in the instant Cr.M.P., be allowed. 5. Learned Spl.P.P. appearing for the State fairly concedes that the sample was received by the Food Analyst on 30.08.2021 and he has furnished the report on 01.10.2021 but submits that the time period of fourteen (14) days provided under Section 42 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is not mandatory but directory in nature, hence, for the violation of the same, entire criminal proceeding ought not be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 6. Having heard the rival submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record, it is pertinent to mention here Section 42 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 which reads as under:- "42. Procedure for launching prosecution.- (1)Xxxx. (2) The Food Analyst after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer shall analyse the sample and send the analysis report mentioning method of sampling and analysis within fourteen days to Designated Officer with a copy to Commissioner of Food Safety." categorically provides for furnishing of the analyst report within fourteen (14) days from the date of receipt of the sample. (2025:JHHC:14957) In this regard, it is relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon'ble Madras High Court in the case of V. Ramesh & Others vs. State Represented by Food Safety Officer passed in Crl.O.P. No.4038 of 2021 dated 28.03.2023. 9. Keeping in view the ratio of the said judgment of Hon'ble Madras High Court, with which this Court is in agreement, this Court is of the considered (2025:JHHC:14957) view that since the Food Analyst has not submitted the report within the stipulated period of fourteen (14) days; as provided for under Section 42 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006; the launching of the complaint is not proper and in view of the violation of the stipulated period which is mandatory in nature, this Court has no hesitation in holding that the continuation of the criminal proceeding including the order taking cognizance dated 17.08.2022 in connection with Complaint Case No.5124 of 2022 will amount to abuse of process of law.
